verdicts.note: The evidence covers reproductive policy only: a platform plank on abortion, contraception and IVF access [S3] and a Planned Parenthood endorsement [S1]. The dossier records no statement on gender identity, LGBTQ+ protections or trans participation in sports (no I-638 statement found), which are the axis's other components and its general-ballot focus. The direction is clear, but evidence on one sub-area does not support placing him fully at the pole; +1 at medium fits the evidence.

Rests on two generic pledges from his issues page and statement ('increase housing supply', 'oppose regulations that artificially inflate costs') [S3][S1] with no specific proposal (no GMA, energy-code, permitting or zoning position). The direction is clear, but slogan-level evidence does not support placing him fully at the pole, especially when the incumbent, scored -1, has a concrete deregulatory record.

Evidence is a single generic website line ('stands firmly behind our law enforcement officers', support for community policing funding, oppose policies that 'undermine public safety') [S3], with no position on drug possession, encampments, staffing or treatment. As in the Grant LD13 refutation, a generic priority statement places him loosely toward enforcement but does not support medium confidence.

The only concrete evidence is the Highway 101 roundabouts remark [S6], which Bernbaum also made at the same forum and was scored -1 for; the other citations are generic phrasing ('local voices shape the policies', policy reflecting 'the people who actually live here') [S1][S3]. The dossier has no position on GMA, state housing mandates or regional authorities. -1 at medium fits the evidence and keeps the two candidates consistent.
